'''Pramod Venkatesh Mahajan''' (30 October 1949 – 3 May 2006,  {{Pronunciation|Pramod_Mahajan.wav}}) was an Indian politician from [[Maharashtra]].<ref>{{cite news |url =https://theprint.in/theprint-profile/pramod-mahajan-bjps-master-strategist-and-troubleshooter-before-amit-shah/413418/|title =Pramod Mahajan, BJP's master strategist and troubleshooter before Amit Shah|publisher =[[ThePrint]]|quote =Pramod Mahajan was the brain behind the Shiv Sena-BJP alliance in Maharashtra and was believed to be the only person Bal Thackeray trusted in the party|date =3 May 2020|website =theprint.in|author =Revathi Krishnan|access-date =3 May 2020}}</ref> A second-generation leader of the [[Bharatiya Janata Party]] (BJP), he belonged to a group of relatively young "[[technocratic]]" leaders.

He was a member of the [[Rajya Sabha]] and a General Secretary of his party. He contested only [[Lok Sabha]] elections from Mumbai – North East constituency. He won in 1996 but lost in 1998. As Prime Minister [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee]]'s telecommunications minister between 2001 and 2003, he played a major role in India's cellular revolution. He was widely seen as a successful Parliamentary Affairs minister due to his good relations with members of political parties across the ideological spectrum.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://rajyasabha.nic.in/kiosk/whoswho/alpha_m1.htm | title = Mahajan, Shri Pramod. Biographical sketch | publisher = Rajya Sabha | access-date = 2 September 2006|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060430014535/http://rajyasabha.nic.in/kiosk/whoswho/alpha_m1.htm |archive-date = 30 April 2006}}</ref>

On 22 April 2006, he was murdered by his brother Pravin Mahajan over a family dispute. He succumbed to his injury 13 days later. Pravin was sentenced to lifetime imprisonment by the court in 2007.

==Early life==
Pramod Mahajan was born to Venkatesh Devidas Mahajan and Prabhavati Venkatesh Mahajan in [[Mahbubnagar]], [[Telangana]], [[India]] in a [[Deshastha Brahmin]] family.<ref>{{cite news | title =BJP loses its master strategist | work = Rediff News | date = 3 May 2006 | url = http://www.rediff.com/news/2006/may/03mahajan4.htm | quote= "Pramod Mahajan's was a truly meteoric rise in the country's political landscape...The wily 56-year old Deshastha Brahmin was not only the Bharatiya Janata Party's master strategist...}}</ref> The Mahajan family had migrated from their home in Mahajan gully in [[Dharashiv]] to [[Ambajogai]] and were staying in a rented house in Mangalwar Peth. Mahajan spent his childhood in Ambejogai. He was the second child of his parents, with two brothers Prakash and Pravin, and two sisters Pratibha and Pradnya. His father died when he was 21. He attended Yogeshwari Vidyalaya and Mahavidyalaya in [[Beed]] district of [[Maharashtra]] and studied at the [[Ranade Institute for Journalism]], [[Pune]]. He obtained bachelor's degrees in Physics and Journalism and a post graduate degree in Political Science.<ref name=dna>{{cite news | title =He is BJP's tomorrow man | work = Daily News and Analysis | date = 23 April 2006 | url = http://www.dnaindia.com/report.asp?NewsID=1025614 | access-date = 2 September 2006 }}</ref> He with his future brother-in-law [[Gopinath Munde]] studied in Swami Ramanand Teerth College, [[Ambajogai]], Maharashtra. He passed Maharashtra Certified Typewriting from former Mahajan Typewriting Institute, [[Ambajogai]].

His love for theatre brought him close to Rekha Hamine, whom he courted and married on 11 March 1972. They have two children, daughter [[Poonam Mahajan Rao|Poonam]] and son [[Rahul Mahajan]]. Both his children are trained pilots. His daughter is married to Anand Rao Vajendla, an industrialist from Hyderabad.<ref name=dna /> Until his death he resided in [[Worli]] and shared the same floor of the apartment building with [[Gopinath Munde]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-06-04 |title=Brothers-in-law Gopinath Munde and Pramod Mahajan gone at their peak |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/brothers-in-law-gopinath-munde-and-pramod-mahajan-gone-at-their-peak/articleshow/36018935.cms |access-date=2025-10-16 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

He worked as an English teacher at the Kholeshwar College in Ambejogai between 1971 and 1974 before joining active politics during the [[Indian Emergency|emergency]].<ref name=dna />

==Political career==
Mahajan was a member of [[Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh]] (RSS) since childhood, but he actively got involved when he worked as a sub-editor of its [[Marathi language|Marathi]] Newspaper, ''[[Tarun Bharat]]'' in 1970 and 1971. He quit his job as a school teacher and became a full-time [[RSS pracharak]] in 1974.<ref>
{{cite news |author=Priya Sahgal |title=Flair and flamboyance – Pramod Mahajan: Fastest rising leader of his generation in BJP |newspaper=India Today |date=8 May 2006 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/cover-story/story/20060508-pramod-mahajan-fastest-rising-leader-of-his-generation-in-bjp-783325-2006-05-07 |access-date=7 October 2014}}</ref>

He took part in the agitation against the [[Indian Emergency (1975–77)|state of emergency]] imposed by the then Prime Minister [[Indira Gandhi]] and was incarcerated in the Nashik central jail until it was lifted.  He was one of the select batch of RSS workers co-opted into the BJP and was the general secretary of the party's state unit till 1985. Between 1983 and 1985, he was also the All India Secretary of his party. After unsuccessfully contesting the 1984 [[Lok Sabha]] elections, he became the president of the All India [[Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha]] in 1986, a position he held again between 1990 and 1992. By virtue of his organizational skills and hard work, he rose to a prominent position, first in the [[Maharashtra state]] BJP and then at the national level.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

Mahajan's aspirations were always national, but he also did a significant amount of work in building up his party's fortunes in his home state of Maharashtra. In this, he was partnered with his childhood friend-turned brother-in-law [[Gopinath Munde]] (who is married to his sister Pradnya). Mahajan was responsible for his party's alliance with the [[Shiv Sena (1966–2022)|Shiv Sena]]. The alliance went on to win the state assembly elections in 1995 and ruled till 1999. Munde was the deputy chief minister in that government.<ref>{{cite news | last = Firdaus | first = Ashraf | title = How Mahajan kept the BJP-Sena together | publisher = Rediff | date = 4 May 2006 | url = http://www.rediff.com/news/2006/may/04mahajan.htm | access-date = 7 September 2006  }}</ref>

Mahajan came to play a vital role during the coalition era of the late 1980s. He rose to national prominence when he helped organize BJP President [[Lal Krishna Advani]]'s ''[[Ram Rath Yatra]]'' in 1990.<ref>{{cite news |title=Advani, the original Rath Yatri of Indian politics |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/india/advani-the-original-rath-yatri-of-indian-politics-3-2878776 |work=Deccan Herald |language=en}}</ref>

Despite being credited with responsibility for his party's numerous election victories, Mahajan rarely contested or won popular elections himself. He had been elected to Parliament many times, but mostly through the Rajya Sabha, the indirectly elected upper house. He served in the Rajya Sabha in 1986–92, 1992–96, 1998–2004 and for the last time in 2004.<ref>{{cite web | url= http://164.100.47.5/Newmembers/alphabeticallist_all_terms.aspx | title = List of Rajya Sabha members | publisher = Rajya Sabha Secretariat | access-date = 30 December 2009 }}</ref> He was elected to the Lok Sabha once in 1996 from [[Mumbai North East (Lok Sabha constituency)|Mumbai North East]].<ref>{{cite web |title=IndiaVotes PC: Mumbai North East 1996 |url=https://www.indiavotes.com/lok-sabha-details/1996/maharashtra/mumbai-north-east/5267/30/11 |website=IndiaVotes}}</ref>



==Government==
The [[Lok Sabha]] elections of 1996 brought the BJP to power and Mahajan was appointed Defence Minister in [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee|Vajpayee]]'s 13-day ministry. When the BJP returned to power in 1998, he was first appointed as advisor to the Prime Minister. He resigned from that post and stood for Rajya Sabha elections in July 1998. He won and in December 1998, he was appointed the Minister for Information and Broadcasting, and Food Processing. A year later, in October 1999, he was moved to Parliamentary Affairs and Water Resources. He relinquished Water Resources a month later in November and took charge of Information Technology (in addition to Parliamentary Affairs).

In 2001, he was appointed<ref>{{cite web | year = 2002 | url = http://www.rediff.com/money/2002/sep/02inter.htm | title = 'Our telecom services don't match world standards yet' | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 26 April 2006}}</ref> to the Communications ministry under controversial circumstances. The earlier telecom policy of the government, formulated in 1994,<ref>{{cite web | year = 1994 | url = http://www.trai.gov.in/ntp1994.htm.htm | title = National Telecom Policy, 1994 | publisher = Telecom regulatory authority of India | access-date = 26 April 2006|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060220065732/http://www.trai.gov.in/ntp1994.htm.htm <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 20 February 2006}}</ref> had allowed private participation in cellular telephony after open bidding, on payment of a license fee determined through the bidding. However, after winning the contracts the telecom companies found themselves unable to pay the fixed license fees, supposedly because the victors fell victim to the [[Winner's curse]].<ref>{{cite web | year = 2003 | url = http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/2003/11/11/stories/2003111100030800.htm | title =  How telecom wires got so tangled | work = Business Line
 | access-date = 26 April 2006}}</ref> The then Minister for Communications, [[Jagmohan]] attempted tough action<ref>{{cite web | year = 1999
 | url = http://www.rediff.com/computer/1999/jan/18dues.htm | title =  Jagmohan wags a warning finger at telecom companies | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 26 April 2006}}</ref> against the defaulting companies, but was sacked.<ref>{{cite web | year = 1999 | url = http://www.rediff.com/computer/1999/jun/09sack.htm | title =  A man slighted | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 26 April 2006
}}</ref> After this, Prime Minister Vajpayee himself took over the cabinet portfolio (with [[Ram Vilas Paswan]] as minister of state) and oversaw the formulation of the New Telecom Policy of 1999.<ref>{{cite web | year = 1999 | url = http://www.trai.gov.in/npt1999.htm | title = National Telecom Policy, 1999 | publisher = Telecom regulatory authority of India | access-date = 26 April 2006|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20060408160931/http://www.trai.gov.in/npt1999.htm <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 8 April 2006}}</ref> The policy replaced fixed license fees with a revenue sharing agreement, a move that was widely criticized<ref>{{cite web | year = 1999 | url = http://www.hinduonnet.com/fline/fl1617/16170060.htm | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20011220052903/http://www.hinduonnet.com/fline/fl1617/16170060.htm | url-status = usurped | archive-date = 20 December 2001 | title =  The telecom tangle | publisher = Hindu on the net | access-date = 26 April 2006}}</ref> for changing rules midway and causing loss of revenue to the government. Mahajan, who succeeded to the post in August 2001, after a cabinet reshuffle (that also merged the department of Information technology with the Telecommunications portfolio) had the task of implementing this policy.

During his tenure, the number of new telephone connections enjoyed unprecedented growth and rentals fell by a large amount. However, he was also accused of favouring [[Reliance Infocomm]] by allowing it to offer full nationwide mobility through [[Wireless local loop|WLL]] without payment of the required license fees.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.flonnet.com/fl2301/stories/20060127004603000.htm |title=Seeking accountability |publisher=Frontline on the net |accessdate=26 April 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060326180027/http://www.flonnet.com/fl2301/stories/20060127004603000.htm |archive-date=26 March 2006}}</ref>

He was also involved in a dispute<ref>{{cite web | year = 2002 | url = http://www.tribuneindia.com/2002/20020605/nation.htm#3 | title =   Arun Shourie hits back at Mahajan | work = The Tribune | access-date = 26 April 2006}}</ref> with the then [[Disinvestment]] minister [[Arun Shourie]] over the privatization of [[VSNL]]. There was speculation that he was a casualty of the silent intra-party battle between Vajpayee and Advani {{Citation needed|date=February 2007}}. Shourie succeeded him to the Communications portfolio.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2003 | url = http://www.tribuneindia.com/2003/20030131/main2.htm | title =   Shourie warns telecom players | work = The Tribune | access-date = 26 April 2006}}</ref> Mahajan was appointed the General Secretary of the BJP. He contested media speculation that this was a demotion, saying that there were no differences between him and the party and that he had just changed positions from chariot rider to charioteer.{{Citation needed|date=February 2007}}

== Allegations for role in Shivani Bhatnagar's death ==
Mahajan was accused of orchestrating the murder of former Indian Express journalist [[Shivani Bhatnagar]] by Madhu Sharma, the wife of IPS officer Ravi Kant Sharma who was an accused in the murder and in police custody.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2003 | url = http://www.rediff.com/news/2003/nov/03sld4.htm | title = Shivani Bhatnagar Case | publisher = Rediff India | access-date = 3 May 2006}}</ref>

Bhatnagar was murdered on 23 January 1999. The investigation had gone on for three years and was out of the media spotlight till Sharma's arrest.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2002 | url = http://www.hinduonnet.com/fline/fl1918/19180200.htm | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20030430002006/http://www.hinduonnet.com/fline/fl1918/19180200.htm | url-status = usurped | archive-date = 30 April 2003 | title = A sordid affair | work = Frontline | access-date = 3 May 2006}}</ref> His motive for the murder, according to the Delhi Police, was that he had fathered Bhatnagar's child and was under pressure from her to marry him. Madhu made statements in the press claiming that it was, in fact, Mahajan who had the affair and was the actual father. She challenged him to a DNA test. Mahajan agreed to take the test but eventually did not as the Delhi Police dismissed Sharma's claim as an emotional outburst as she was unable to provide any concrete evidence in support of her charges.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

==2003 and 2004 elections==
[[State Assembly elections in India, 2003|Assembly elections]] were held in four Indian states in December 2003 – [[Delhi]], Chhattisgarh, [[Madhya Pradesh]] and [[Rajasthan]]. Mahajan was put in charge of Rajasthan.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2003 | url =  http://in.rediff.com/news/2003/jul/18bjp1.htm | title = We'll have a 4–0 lead | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 1 May 2006}}</ref> The BJP consciously chose to play down the [[Hindutva]] platform.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2003 | url = http://www.rediff.com/election/2003/nov/29inter1.htm | title =   Hindutva not to be poll issue: BJP | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 1 May 2006}}</ref> Nonetheless, the elections turned out to be a resounding victory for the BJP, which won in three of the four states.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2003 | url = http://in.rediff.com/election/poll03.htm | title =   The Assembly elections 2003 homepage | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 1 May 2006}}</ref> Emboldened by this success, [[Atal Bihari Vajpayee|Vajpayee]] called early [[2004 Indian general elections|elections]] in 2004 and Mahajan was given charge of the campaign. However, the BJP performed unexpectedly poorly in them, losing power to the [[Indian National Congress]]. Mahajan personally accepted responsibility for this defeat.<ref>{{cite web | year = 2004
 | url =  http://www.rediff.com/election/2004/may/13pramod.htm | title =   Mahajan accepts blame for BJP debacle | work = Rediff.com
 | access-date = 1 May 2006}}</ref>

==Death==
On the morning of 22 April 2006, Mahajan's estranged younger brother, Pravin shot him with his licensed [[Browning Arms Company|.32 Browning pistol]] inside the former's apartment in Mumbai following a dispute. Four bullets were fired. Mahajan was taken to the [[P. D. Hinduja National Hospital and Medical Research Centre|Hinduja Hospital]] where he was operated upon. Liver specialist [[Mohammed Rela|Mohamed {{sic|hide=y|Re|la}}]] flew in from London to treat him.<ref>[http://in.rediff.com/news/2006/apr/23rela.htm The specialist who will treat Mahajan] – Rediff News 23 April 2006</ref> After struggling for his life for 13 days, Mahajan suffered from a cardiac arrest and died on 3 May 2006 at 16:10.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://in.rediff.com/news/2006/may/03mahajan1.htm | year = 2006 | title = Pramod Mahajan passes away | work = Rediff.com | access-date = 3 May 2006}}</ref> He was given a state funeral at the [[Shivaji Park]] crematorium in [[Dadar]], Mumbai on 4 May 2006.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120308234531/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2006-05-04/india/27797341_1_pravin-cremation-grounds-hinduja-hospital State funeral given to Pramod Mahajan]</ref>

==Aftermath==
Pravin surrendered at the [[Mumbai Police|Worli Police Station in Mumbai]] after the shooting. The police claimed that it was a premeditated attack born out of resentment built up over a long time. Pravin accused his brother of "ignoring and humiliating him, and not giving him his due". He also felt neglected and suffered from an [[inferiority complex]] because he was the poorer younger brother of a much famous elder brother.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.ndtv.com/template/template.asp?template=mahajanshot&slug=Attack+on+Pramod+premeditated%3A+Police&id=19249&callid=0&category=National| title = Attack on Pramod premeditated: Police| publisher = NDTV| access-date = 24 April 2006}}</ref> Pravin was charged with murder under Sec. 302 of the [[Indian Penal Code|Indian Penal Code (IPC)]].<ref>[http://www.outlookindia.com/pti_news.asp?id=382184 Chargesheet changed from Attempt to Murder to Murder] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070311125528/http://www.outlookindia.com/pti_news.asp?id=382184 |date=11 March 2007 }}</ref> However, Pravin told the court that he had not fired the bullets at his brother. On 18 December 2007, Pravin was sentenced to [[life imprisonment]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2007-12-18/india/27961695_1_pramod-mahajan-pravin-mahajan-bjp-leader |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019021052/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2007-12-18/india/27961695_1_pramod-mahajan-pravin-mahajan-bjp-leader |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 October 2012 | title=Pravin gets life term for killing Pramod Mahajan |access-date = 19 December 2007 |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=18 December 2007}}</ref> Pravin died on 3 March 2010 due to [[brain haemorrhage]]. He was on parole when he suffered the stroke and was hospitalised.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110811045329/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2010-03-03/mumbai/28120015_1_pravin-mahajan-pramod-mahajan-worli-police Pravin Mahajan dies of brain hemorrhage] – The Times of India 3 March 2010</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article138895.ece|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121127215704/http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/article138895.ece|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 November 2012|title=Pravin Mahajan is dead |website=[[The Hindu]] |access-date=3 March 2010}}</ref>
